note: Belize: nationals of Barbados, Dominica and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines move freely; the listed others enter without a visa for 180 days (the United States), 90 (Russia in 180) or 30 (Chile, listed under both 90 and 30, is taken at 90). Everyone else needs a visa; a 30-day entry on a US, Canadian or Schengen multiple-entry visa, and the repatriation fee asked of Bangladesh, China, India, Pakistan and Sri Lanka, aren't modelled. Read from Wikipedia's copy. Checked on 2026-11-03 against the Immigration and Nationality Services' own table (Visa Who Qualify): it names each country as needing a visa or not, with a length where it differs from the 30 days its page gives every visitor; it corrected Wikipedia's copy, read before, on Zimbabwe (a visa) and Russia (no length of its own, so 30 days, not 90 in 180). It doesn't name Slovakia or Slovenia, and doesn't speak of the free movement of Barbados', Dominica's and Saint Vincent's citizens: those stand on Wikipedia's copy. The territories it names as needing no visa are their states' passports here.
